question.question:
Use exact arithmetic. A firm follows a strict residual dividend policy. Next year's capital budget is 100 USD million and the target equity ratio is 40 percent of the capital budget, so the equity required equals the capital budget times that ratio. Base net income is 95 USD million, and a one-time after-tax item changes it by 5 percent of base net income (a negative value is a loss, a positive value is a gain), giving adjusted net income. The signed surplus equals adjusted net income minus the equity required; a negative surplus means a shortfall. Any positive surplus is paid out entirely as dividends. If the surplus is negative, the firm issues new equity for the full shortfall and pays a zero dividend. Report the total dividend paid in USD million.

Answer format: return only the exact numeric value interpreted in `usd_million`, using finite-decimal notation when it terminates in base 10 and an irreducible `numerator/denominator` fraction otherwise, with no unit label or additional text.

slots.description: Equity portion of the capital budget at the target equity ratio
Net income after the signed one-time after-tax item
Adjusted net income minus equity required; negative means shortfall
New equity raised to cover any shortfall; zero if no shortfall
